craft_claim: Grim weight becomes art rather than mere misery only when the text gives the reader a frame through which violation and loss can be appraised; negative affect with no meaning-frame reads as noise, not tragedy.

supporting_evidence.note: Park's integrative review distinguishes global meaning (beliefs, goals, sense of coherence) from situational meaning, and models meaning-making as the attempt to reconcile the two after a stressful event; adjustment depends on whether some meanings are made. This is the basis for saying grim material must be appraisable, not merely awful.

supporting_evidence.location: Handbook of Theories of Social Psychology, Vol. 1, pp. 289-308
supporting_evidence.note: Feelings-as-information theory holds that affective states inform appraisal and processing style. Negative affect signals a problematic situation and tends to elicit more systematic, vigilant processing, which is why a grim register can command careful attention rather than mere aversion.

counterevidence.note: Section B's honest null states that no study isolates grim tone and that Park's model is drawn from stress-adjustment research, so the extension from post-event meaning-making to reader response in a sustained grim register is writer-inference, and the claim's exceptions allow refusal of meaning to function as the appraisable frame.

scope: Fiction, memoir, essay, and any long-form prose that sustains a negative register.
exceptions: Deliberately absurdist or nihilist art may stage the refusal of meaning as its frame; the refusal itself is the appraisable gesture.
Reportage or witness testimony may owe fidelity to meaninglessness and should not be forced into consolation.
